subject: SDG Weekly Compass - Week of 2026-09-07
overview_zh: 技术与治理的修复都在加速，但谁来为外部性买单仍未清楚。

items.title_en: Analysis: UK solar power hits record high over summer 2026
items.summary_zh: 英国太阳能发电在极端高温与长日照条件下创下夏季纪录，说明电力系统中的可再生能源部署已开始把气候冲击转化为供给增量；文章隐含的政策含义是，电网调度、储能和并网规则必须同步升级，才能把“天气红利”稳定转化为系统韧性，而不是只在短期内抬高发电峰值。
items.core_argument_zh: 英国太阳能发电在极端高温与长日照条件下创下夏季纪录，说明电力系统中的可再生能源部署已开始把气候冲击转化为供给增量；文章隐含的政策含义是，电网调度、储能和并网规则必须同步升级，才能把“天气红利”稳定转化为系统韧性，而不是只在短期内抬高发电峰值。
items.core_argument_en: UK solar generation set a summer record under extreme heat and long daylight, showing that renewable deployment is beginning to turn climate stress into supply gains; the policy implication is that grid dispatch, storage, and interconnection rules must advance in parallel so weather-driven gains become system resilience rather than a short-lived output spike.
items.why_now_zh: 这篇分析回应的是2026年夏季高温、日照异常和发电纪录同时出现的窗口，说明“更多太阳能”不再只是装机故事，而是电力系统适配极端天气的治理问题。它也把政策讨论从扩张速度推向系统整合。
items.why_now_en: The piece responds to the 2026 summer when record heat, unusual sunshine, and record output coincided, showing that ‘more solar’ is no longer just an installation story but a governance problem of system adaptation to extremes. It shifts the debate from capacity growth to system integration.
items.agenda_position_zh: 它处在英国电力市场改革与净零执行框架的交汇处，直接触及并网、储能和需求侧响应的政策排序。
items.agenda_position_en: It sits at the intersection of UK power-market reform and net-zero implementation, directly affecting the policy sequencing of interconnection, storage, and demand-side response.
items.why_it_matters_zh: 这篇分析回应的是2026年夏季高温、日照异常和发电纪录同时出现的窗口，说明“更多太阳能”不再只是装机故事，而是电力系统适配极端天气的治理问题。它也把政策讨论从扩张速度推向系统整合。

items.title_en: How this summer’s heat and drought impacted crops in Europe – in six charts
items.summary_zh: 欧洲农业面对的不是单一气象冲击，而是热浪、干旱、野火与能源价格、化肥供应和燃料成本叠加形成的复合风险；文章指向的机制是，农业产出波动已从自然灾害问题转为供应链、投入品价格和气候适应政策共同塑造的制度性脆弱性，因此需要把作物保险、灌溉投资、化肥替代和食品价格缓冲纳入同一治理框架。
items.core_argument_zh: 欧洲农业面对的不是单一气象冲击，而是热浪、干旱、野火与能源价格、化肥供应和燃料成本叠加形成的复合风险；文章指向的机制是，农业产出波动已从自然灾害问题转为供应链、投入品价格和气候适应政策共同塑造的制度性脆弱性，因此需要把作物保险、灌溉投资、化肥替代和食品价格缓冲纳入同一治理框架。
items.core_argument_en: European agriculture is not facing a single weather shock but a compound risk in which heat, drought, and wildfires interact with energy prices, fertilizer supply, and fuel costs; the article’s mechanism is that output volatility has become an institutional vulnerability shaped by supply chains, input prices, and adaptation policy, requiring crop insurance, irrigation investment, fertilizer substitution, and food-price buffers to be governed together.
items.why_now_zh: 这篇文章正好回应今夏极端天气结束后各国开始评估收成损失、粮价压力和农业救助的时间点。它把短期歉收放回到欧洲粮食安全和适应融资的中期议程中。
items.why_now_en: The article lands as governments begin assessing harvest losses, food-price pressure, and farm relief after the summer extremes. It moves short-term crop failures into Europe’s medium-term food-security and adaptation-finance agenda.
items.agenda_position_zh: 它嵌入欧盟农业与食品安全政策、适应战略以及下一轮气候损失与损害讨论的交叉处。
items.agenda_position_en: It sits at the intersection of EU agriculture and food-security policy, adaptation strategy, and the next round of loss-and-damage debates.

items.title_en: The state of the EU’s climate agenda: into autumn 2026 and beyond
items.summary_zh: E3G把欧盟气候议程放进“独立时刻”与脆弱性政治之中，强调贸易、技术、安全和极端天气正在迫使欧盟把气候政策从单一减排框架转向更广义的战略韧性框架；其核心含义是，若不把工业政策、能源安全和气候目标协调起来，欧盟将难以在秋季政治窗口中维持政策一致性与执行力。

terms.explanation_zh: 国家、国际组织和非国家行为体围绕共同问题形成规则、协调行动和分配责任的机制。

items.core_argument_zh: E3G把欧盟气候议程放进“独立时刻”与脆弱性政治之中，强调贸易、技术、安全和极端天气正在迫使欧盟把气候政策从单一减排框架转向更广义的战略韧性框架；其核心含义是，若不把工业政策、能源安全和气候目标协调起来，欧盟将难以在秋季政治窗口中维持政策一致性与执行力。
items.core_argument_en: E3G places the EU climate agenda within a politics of independence and vulnerability, arguing that trade, technology, security, and extreme weather are pushing climate policy beyond a narrow emissions frame toward strategic resilience; the implication is that without aligning industrial policy, energy security, and climate goals, the EU will struggle to sustain coherence and implementation through the autumn window.
items.why_now_zh: 这篇评论直接对应欧盟进入秋季立法和政策协调期的时点，也回应了近年安全与产业压力对气候优先序的挤压。它的时间性不在于新数据，而在于政治排序已经改变。
items.why_now_en: The commentary directly targets the EU’s autumn legislative and coordination period, responding to the way security and industrial pressures have crowded the climate agenda. Its timing is political rather than data-driven: the hierarchy of priorities has already shifted.
items.agenda_position_zh: 它处在欧盟委员会“独立时刻”叙事、成员国竞争性优先序和下一阶段气候实施的交汇点上。
items.agenda_position_en: It sits at the intersection of the Commission’s ‘independence moment’ narrative, member-state priority competition, and the next phase of climate implementation.
items.why_it_matters_zh: 这篇评论直接对应欧盟进入秋季立法和政策协调期的时点，也回应了近年安全与产业压力对气候优先序的挤压。它的时间性不在于新数据，而在于政治排序已经改变。

readings.title: Gatekeeping the Greenland ice sheet: climate change data and the “upstream” production of global governance objects
readings.note_zh: 文章提出“守门”（gatekeeping）概念，强调全球治理对象不是在发表结果时才成形，而是在数据被采集、筛选和初步分析的上游阶段就已被权力关系塑造。作者通过格陵兰冰盖冰芯研究的跨点民族志，说明国家与科学机构如何控制原始气候数据的流动与内容，并把数据主权（data sovereignty）问题前移到知识生产的起点。
readings.note_en: The article develops ‘gatekeeping’ to show that global governance objects are shaped not at the point of published results, but upstream when data are scoped, extracted, and preliminarily analyzed. Through multi-sited ethnography of Greenland ice-core science, the author shows how states and scientific institutions control the flow and content of raw climate data and moves data sovereignty to the start of knowledge production.
readings.methodology_zh: 作者采用多点民族志（multi-sited ethnography），结合参与式观察与半结构式访谈，追踪格陵兰、德国和丹麦的冰芯科学实践。
readings.method_en: The author uses multi-sited ethnography, combining participant observation and semi-structured interviews across Greenland, Germany, and Denmark, to trace ice-core science in practice.
readings.today_connection_zh: 可与本期 Carbon Brief 关于英国太阳能纪录高位一文对读：两者都提示，能源与气候治理的关键不只在结果端，更在数据、基础设施和制度门槛如何被提前设定。
readings.today_connection_en: Read alongside this issue’s Carbon Brief piece on UK solar’s record output: both show that energy and climate governance are shaped not only at the results stage, but by how data, infrastructure, and institutional thresholds are set upstream.

research_directions.question_en: Who controls raw climate data in governance settings?

research_directions.question_zh: 上游知识如何塑造政策？
research_directions.question_en: How does upstream knowledge production shape policy outcomes?

readings.abstract_en: In this article, I develop the concept of “gatekeeping” as it is exerted in the “upstream” of knowledge production. “Upstream” denotes the stage of knowledge production where unprocessed data is scoped, extracted, and preliminarily analyzed, before it later—“downstream”—is published as results on the basis of which political decisions are made. The focus on the upstream of knowledge production and how it is gatekept is an argument to prompt theoretical work on global governance objects to pay attention to the physical data that underlies the formation of epistemic objects. Moreover, the concept of gatekeeping speaks to scholarship concerned with data sovereignty by showing how gatekeeping as a mechanism of control of raw climate data is also exerted by non-sovereign actors or by multiple state actors simultaneously. By following climate scientists around as they scope, extract, and analyze ice cores from the Greenland ice sheet, I show how climate science is full of institutional hierarchies, mutually exclusive scientific interests, and power struggles “inside” science with direct effects on the flow and content of knowledge produced. Conceptualizing gatekeeping as it is exerted by state actors and scientific institutions contributes to our understanding of how power, hierarchy, and political interests are imprinted on climate science from the point of extraction of its physical data. The article follows ice core science ethnographically and asks how and by whom data is extracted from the Greenland ice sheet, building on participant observation and semi-structured interviews during multi-sited fieldwork across Greenland, Germany, and Denmark.

overview_en: Both technical fixes and governance repairs are accelerating, but who pays for the externalities remains unresolved.
weekly_thread_zh: 本期线索都在问同一件事：气候风险上升时，政策是把问题嵌入现有制度，还是推动制度本身重组？
weekly_thread_en: This issue converges on one question: as climate risks intensify, should policy embed the problem into existing institutions or reorganize the institutions themselves?

classic_readings.title: Gatekeeping the Greenland ice sheet: climate change data and the “upstream” production of global governance objects
classic_readings.note_zh: 文章提出“守门”（gatekeeping）概念，强调全球治理对象不是在发表结果时才成形，而是在数据被采集、筛选和初步分析的上游阶段就已被权力关系塑造。作者通过格陵兰冰盖冰芯研究的跨点民族志，说明国家与科学机构如何控制原始气候数据的流动与内容，并把数据主权（data sovereignty）问题前移到知识生产的起点。
classic_readings.note_en: The article develops ‘gatekeeping’ to show that global governance objects are shaped not at the point of published results, but upstream when data are scoped, extracted, and preliminarily analyzed. Through multi-sited ethnography of Greenland ice-core science, the author shows how states and scientific institutions control the flow and content of raw climate data and moves data sovereignty to the start of knowledge production.
classic_readings.methodology_zh: 作者采用多点民族志（multi-sited ethnography），结合参与式观察与半结构式访谈，追踪格陵兰、德国和丹麦的冰芯科学实践。
classic_readings.method_en: The author uses multi-sited ethnography, combining participant observation and semi-structured interviews across Greenland, Germany, and Denmark, to trace ice-core science in practice.
classic_readings.today_connection_zh: 可与本期 Carbon Brief 关于英国太阳能纪录高位一文对读：两者都提示，能源与气候治理的关键不只在结果端，更在数据、基础设施和制度门槛如何被提前设定。
classic_readings.today_connection_en: Read alongside this issue’s Carbon Brief piece on UK solar’s record output: both show that energy and climate governance are shaped not only at the results stage, but by how data, infrastructure, and institutional thresholds are set upstream.

research_directions.question_en: Who controls raw climate data in governance settings?

research_directions.question_zh: 上游知识如何塑造政策？
research_directions.question_en: How does upstream knowledge production shape policy outcomes?

classic_readings.abstract_en: In this article, I develop the concept of “gatekeeping” as it is exerted in the “upstream” of knowledge production. “Upstream” denotes the stage of knowledge production where unprocessed data is scoped, extracted, and preliminarily analyzed, before it later—“downstream”—is published as results on the basis of which political decisions are made. The focus on the upstream of knowledge production and how it is gatekept is an argument to prompt theoretical work on global governance objects to pay attention to the physical data that underlies the formation of epistemic objects. Moreover, the concept of gatekeeping speaks to scholarship concerned with data sovereignty by showing how gatekeeping as a mechanism of control of raw climate data is also exerted by non-sovereign actors or by multiple state actors simultaneously. By following climate scientists around as they scope, extract, and analyze ice cores from the Greenland ice sheet, I show how climate science is full of institutional hierarchies, mutually exclusive scientific interests, and power struggles “inside” science with direct effects on the flow and content of knowledge produced. Conceptualizing gatekeeping as it is exerted by state actors and scientific institutions contributes to our understanding of how power, hierarchy, and political interests are imprinted on climate science from the point of extraction of its physical data. The article follows ice core science ethnographically and asks how and by whom data is extracted from the Greenland ice sheet, building on participant observation and semi-structured interviews during multi-sited fieldwork across Greenland, Germany, and Denmark.
